title: Thermal Transport and Lattice Dynamics in Solid Electrolytes
journal: Ph.D. Dissertation, University of California, Riverside

title: Thermal transport mechanisms in electrolytes for all-solid-state batteries
summary: How do solid electrolytes carry heat, and what limits their thermal conductivity? This review connects evidence across oxides, sulfides, and halides, examining lattice dynamics, diffuson transport, and the effects of disorder, porosity, and aging on battery thermal management.
figure_alt: Overview of thermal transport in solid electrolytes, relating intrinsic lattice dynamics, extrinsic material effects, and the relationship between thermal and ionic transport.
figure_caption: Graphical overview supplied by the author: mechanisms and material factors governing thermal transport in solid electrolytes.

title: Origin of intrinsically low thermal conductivity in a garnet-type solid electrolyte: Linking lattice and ionic dynamics with thermal transport
authors: **Wang, Y.**, Su, Y., Carrete, J., Zhang, H., Wu, N., Li, Y., Li, H., He, J., Xu, Y., Guo, S., Cai, Q., Abernathy, D. L., Williams, T., Kravchyk, K. V., Kovalenko, M. V., Madsen, G. K. H., Li, C., & Chen, X.
summary: Why does a crystalline garnet electrolyte conduct heat like a glass? Combining single-crystal growth, neutron scattering, and calculations, we connect low thermal conductivity to optical phonon modes and strong anharmonicity. A two-channel model captures contributions from propagating phonons and diffusons.
figure_alt: LLZTO crystal structure, grown single crystals, elemental maps, microscopy and diffraction images, and temperature-dependent thermal conductivity of single-crystal and polycrystalline samples.
figure_caption: Figure 1 supplied by the author: LLZTO structure, sample characterization, and thermal conductivity. Wang et al., PRX Energy 4, 033004 (2025).

summary: Thermal conductivity, expansion, and heat-capacity measurements reveal strong lattice anharmonicity in polycrystalline LLZTO. We also find that aging increases thermal conductivity at room temperature, highlighting how changes in a solid electrolyte can affect battery heat management.
